exposure: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) program implementation
outcome: Outpatient opioids dispensed at hospital discharge
Hours to first postsurgical solid intake
cohort: The study included 4,689 patients undergoing elective cesarean delivery before and 4,624 patients after ERAS program implementation in a large integrated health care delivery system.
finding: Implementation of an ERAS program for elective cesarean delivery significantly reduced inpatient and outpatient opioid exposure and improved surgical process measures without worsening surgical outcomes.
